rv.q: Together, it has the makings of a quirky West End transfer, in the mould of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button .

Curiously, however, it was not a sponsored walk for charitable causes, but simply a personal decision, made by Harold Fry (Mark Addy), too British and too stubborn to turn back, despite a lack of suitable footwear or, initially at least, as much as a map.

The titular Harold (Mark Addy – wonderful performance) receives a letter from a former work colleague, who he hasn’t seen or heard from for 20 years. She tells him she is dying in a hospice in Berwick-upon-Tweed.
